rows.label: Dunning–Kruger effect
rows.description: cognitive bias in which incompetent people tend to assess themselves as skilled

rows.label: Schrödinger's cat
rows.description: thought experiment

rows.label: Streisand effect
rows.description: phenomenon whereby an attempt to hide, remove, or censor a piece of information has the unintended consequence of publicizing the information more widely, usually facilitated by the Internet

rows.label: Fermi paradox
rows.description: apparent contradiction between the lack of evidence and high probability estimates for the existence of extraterrestrial civilizations

rows.label: Jevons paradox
rows.description: economical theory that increased efficiency in use of a resource also tends to increase consumption of that resource

rows.label: survivorship bias
rows.description: logical error of concentrating on the people or things that made it past some selection process and overlooking those that did not, typically because of the latter's lack of visibility

rows.label: Monty Hall problem
rows.description: mathematical problem

rows.label: pareidolia
rows.description: psychological effect of observing human faces in inanimate objects

rows.label: birthday problem
rows.description: mathematical problem

rows.label: Baader–Meinhof effect
rows.description: cognitive bias

rows.label: Hilbert's paradox of the Grand Hotel
rows.description: thought experiment proposed by David Hilbert

rows.label: Boy or Girl paradox
rows.description: paradox in probability theory

rows.label: paradox of tolerance
rows.description: logical paradox in decision-making theory

rows.label: confirmation bias
rows.description: tendency of people to favor information that confirms their beliefs or hypotheses

rows.label: Zeno's paradoxes
rows.description: set of philosophical problems

rows.label: loss aversion
rows.description: people's tendency to prefer avoiding losses to acquiring equivalent gains, a behavior first identified by Amos Tversky and Daniel Kahneman

rows.label: Barnum effect
rows.description: psychological phenomenon whereby individuals give high accuracy ratings to descriptions of their personality that supposedly are tailored specifically to them, yet which are in fact vague and general enough to apply to a wide range of people

rows.label: Simpson's paradox
rows.description: phenomenon in probability and statistics, in which a trend appears in several different groups of data but disappears or reverses when these groups are combined

rows.label: halo effect
rows.description: tendency for positive impressions of a person, company, brand or product in one area to positively influence one's opinion or feelings in other areas

rows.label: Russell's paradox
rows.description: paradox in set theory concerning the set of all sets not containing themselves

rows.label: serial position effect
rows.description: tendency of a person to recall the first and last items in a series best, and the middle items worst

rows.label: bystander effect
rows.description: social psychological phenomenon in which individuals are less likely to offer help to a victim when other people are present

rows.label: coastline paradox
rows.description: counterintuitive observation that the coastline of a landmass does not have a well-defined length

rows.label: Hawthorne effect
rows.description: type of reactivity in which individuals modify an aspect of their behavior in response to their awareness of being observed

rows.label: gambler's fallacy
rows.description: mistaken belief that more frequent chance events will lead to less frequent chance events, or vice versa, to balance out

rows.label: Stroop effect
rows.description: effect of psychological interference on reaction time

rows.label: Zeigarnik effect
rows.description: psychological phenomena when an activity that has been interrupted may be more readily recalled

rows.label: curse of knowledge
rows.description: cognitive bias that occurs when an individual unknowingly assumes that the others have the same background to understand

rows.label: Moravec's paradox
rows.description: observation that perception requires more computation than reasoning

rows.label: Pygmalion effect
rows.description: phenomenon whereby others’ expectations of a target person affect the target person’s performance

rows.label: Mandela effect
rows.description: phenomenon in which a group of people share a collective false memory of a past event
